key_insight: The paper shows that time-domain measurements can reveal resonant scattering properties of glueballs in lattice gauge theory, enabling quantum simulations to extract continuum resonance information from real-time dynamics.
engineering_relevance: It provides a benchmark-style workflow for near-term quantum hardware, linking circuit design, Trotterized dynamics, and observables that could guide future fault-tolerant simulation studies in particle physics.
method: Classical exact diagonalization of pure SU(3) lattice gauge theory on a line-of-plaquettes geometry.
Real-time simulations plus approximate analytic methods to identify continuum resonance structure in glueball scattering.
Construction of a toy model and deployment on Quantinuum H2-2 with a 14-plaquette chain encoded in 28 qubits.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports successful extraction of the proposed observables in the toy model and a hardware-feasible resonant collision simulation requiring about 25n entangling gates after optimization and compression.
watch_item: The main limitation is that the hardware demonstration is still a toy-model proxy, and the Trotterized circuits may become costly and error-sensitive as system size or Trotter depth increases.
paper_title: Time-Domain Observables for Resonant Scattering in Quantum Simulations of Lattice Gauge Theory
